modules.title: Full-Text Search
modules.goal: Build ranked, language-aware search instead of fragile LIKE patterns.

topics.title: Full-Text Search Basics
topics.simple: FTS text ko tokens aur queries me match karta hai.
topics.pro: Full-text search parses documents into normalized lexemes and matches them against a query, with ranking and highlighting.
points: It handles words, not just substrings.
It supports stemming and stop words.
It can be indexed with GIN.

example.sql: SELECT to_tsvector('simple', 'SQL joins and indexes') @@ to_tsquery('simple', 'join & index');

topics.title: tsvector
topics.simple: tsvector normalized lexemes ka sorted document hai.
topics.pro: A tsvector stores lexemes with positions, which is the document representation used by full-text search.
points: It can be generated or stored.

topics.title: tsquery
topics.simple: tsquery search terms aur boolean operators rakhta hai.
topics.pro: A tsquery combines lexemes with &, |, ! and phrase operators.

topics.title: to_tsvector
topics.simple: to_tsvector document ko searchable form me badalta hai.
topics.pro: to_tsvector(config, text) normalizes a document using a text search configuration.

example.sql: SELECT to_tsvector('english', 'The SQL course covers indexes');

topics.title: to_tsquery
topics.simple: to_tsquery query string ko tsquery banata hai.
topics.pro: to_tsquery parses explicit operators and requires the caller to format the query safely.

topics.title: plainto_tsquery
topics.simple: plainto_tsquery user text ko safe AND query banata hai.
topics.pro: plainto_tsquery turns plain text into a tsquery by ANDing the lexemes, ignoring operators in the input.
points: It is safer for raw input.

topics.title: websearch_to_tsquery
topics.simple: websearch_to_tsquery search-engine style input samajhta hai.
topics.pro: websearch_to_tsquery supports quoted phrases, OR and minus terms without raising syntax errors on ordinary input.
points: It is designed for user input.

topics.title: Match Operator
topics.simple: @@ operator document aur query ko match karta hai.
topics.pro: The @@ operator returns true when a tsvector matches a tsquery.
points: It is the core FTS predicate.
It can use a GIN index.

example.sql: SELECT title FROM courses WHERE to_tsvector('english', title) @@ plainto_tsquery('english', 'sql');

topics.title: Ranking
topics.simple: ts_rank relevance score deta hai.
topics.pro: ts_rank scores matches by term frequency and proximity, allowing the most relevant results first.
points: Weights can favor title over body.

example.sql: SELECT title, ts_rank(to_tsvector('english', title), plainto_tsquery('english', 'sql')) AS rank FROM courses ORDER BY rank DESC;

topics.title: Highlighting
topics.simple: ts_headline matching text ko highlight karta hai.
topics.pro: ts_headline returns a snippet with query terms wrapped in markers, useful for search result previews.
points: It works on the original text.

example.sql: SELECT ts_headline('english', 'SQL joins and indexes are useful', plainto_tsquery('english', 'index'));

topics.title: Dictionaries
topics.simple: Dictionaries token normalization control karte hain.
topics.pro: Text search dictionaries define stop words, stemming and synonym rules for a configuration.
points: They affect both indexing and queries.

topics.title: Stop Words
topics.simple: Stop words common words hote hain jo search me ignore hote hain.
topics.pro: Stop words such as the and and are removed because they add little discriminating value.

topics.title: Stemming
topics.simple: Stemming words ko root form me le aata hai.
topics.pro: Stemming maps variants such as run, runs and running to a shared lexeme, improving recall.

topics.title: GIN Index for FTS
topics.simple: GIN index full-text search ko fast karta hai.
topics.pro: A GIN index on the tsvector expression accelerates @@ queries.
points: Use the same configuration in queries.
It speeds reads but costs writes.

example.sql: CREATE INDEX idx_courses_title_fts ON courses USING gin (to_tsvector('english', title));

topics.title: Search Configuration
topics.simple: Text search configuration language aur rules choose karti hai.
topics.pro: The configuration determines stop words, stemming and dictionary behavior; indexing and querying must use the same one.
points: Store a generated tsvector for control.

topics.title: Phrase Search
topics.simple: Phrase search words ke order aur adjacency ko match karta hai.
topics.pro: The <-> operator requires adjacent lexemes, while <n> allows a distance.

topics.title: Prefix Search
topics.simple: Prefix search partial words match karta hai.
topics.pro: The :* operator matches lexemes with a prefix, useful for search-as-you-type.

topics.title: Common FTS Errors
topics.simple: Config mismatch, wrong operators aur unindexed expressions common errors hain.
topics.pro: Common failures are querying a different configuration than the index, using LIKE for ranking, and forgetting to index the exact expression.

example.sql: SELECT * FROM courses WHERE to_tsvector('english', title) @@ websearch_to_tsquery('english', 'sql');

topics.title: FTS vs LIKE
topics.simple: FTS words aur relevance deta hai; LIKE substrings deta hai.
topics.pro: LIKE is simple substring matching, while full-text search handles stemming, stop words, ranking and large documents.

example.sql: SELECT title FROM courses WHERE title ILIKE '%sql%';

topics.title: Practical Search
topics.simple: Search query, rank aur headline ko combine karo.
topics.pro: A practical search query filters with @@, orders by ts_rank and returns a headline snippet.

example.sql: SELECT title, ts_rank(to_tsvector('english', title), websearch_to_tsquery('english', 'sql')) AS rank FROM courses WHERE to_tsvector('english', title) @@ websearch_to_tsquery('english', 'sql') ORDER BY rank DESC LIMIT 10;

interview.q: Module 23 · Explain Full-Text Search Basics in a production query.
interview.answer: Full-text search parses documents into normalized lexemes and matches them against a query, with ranking and highlighting. Key rules: It handles words, not just substrings. It supports stemming and stop words. It can be indexed with GIN.

interview.q: Module 23 · Explain tsvector in a production query.
interview.answer: A tsvector stores lexemes with positions, which is the document representation used by full-text search. Key rules: It is not plain text. Positions support phrase search. It can be generated or stored.

interview.q: Module 23 · Explain tsquery in a production query.
interview.answer: A tsquery combines lexemes with &, |, ! and phrase operators. Key rules: & means AND. | means OR. ! means NOT.

interview.q: Module 23 · Explain to_tsvector in a production query.
interview.answer: to_tsvector(config, text) normalizes a document using a text search configuration. Key rules: Choose a language config. It lowercases and stems. It removes stop words.

interview.q: Module 23 · Explain to_tsquery in a production query.
interview.answer: to_tsquery parses explicit operators and requires the caller to format the query safely. Key rules: It accepts operators. It can raise syntax errors. Use parameters for user input.

interview.q: Module 23 · Explain plainto_tsquery in a production query.
interview.answer: plainto_tsquery turns plain text into a tsquery by ANDing the lexemes, ignoring operators in the input. Key rules: It is safer for raw input. It uses AND semantics. It removes stop words.

interview.q: Module 23 · Explain websearch_to_tsquery in a production query.
interview.answer: websearch_to_tsquery supports quoted phrases, OR and minus terms without raising syntax errors on ordinary input. Key rules: It is designed for user input. Quotes create phrases. Minus excludes terms.

interview.q: Module 23 · Explain Match Operator in a production query.
interview.answer: The @@ operator returns true when a tsvector matches a tsquery. Key rules: It is the core FTS predicate. It can use a GIN index. Both sides need matching types.

interview.q: Module 23 · Explain Ranking in a production query.
interview.answer: ts_rank scores matches by term frequency and proximity, allowing the most relevant results first. Key rules: Higher is more relevant. Weights can favor title over body. It is not a probability.

interview.q: Module 23 · Explain Highlighting in a production query.
interview.answer: ts_headline returns a snippet with query terms wrapped in markers, useful for search result previews. Key rules: It works on the original text. Markers are configurable. It can be expensive.

interview.q: Module 23 · Explain Dictionaries in a production query.
interview.answer: Text search dictionaries define stop words, stemming and synonym rules for a configuration. Key rules: They are language-specific. They can be customized. They affect both indexing and queries.

interview.q: Module 23 · Explain Stop Words in a production query.
interview.answer: Stop words such as the and and are removed because they add little discriminating value. Key rules: They reduce index size. They can surprise phrase searches. Configurations differ by language.

interview.q: Module 23 · Explain Stemming in a production query.
interview.answer: Stemming maps variants such as run, runs and running to a shared lexeme, improving recall. Key rules: It improves matching. It can over-stem. The language config controls it.

interview.q: Module 23 · Explain GIN Index for FTS in a production query.
interview.answer: A GIN index on the tsvector expression accelerates @@ queries. Key rules: Index the exact expression. Use the same configuration in queries. It speeds reads but costs writes.

interview.q: Module 23 · Explain Search Configuration in a production query.
interview.answer: The configuration determines stop words, stemming and dictionary behavior; indexing and querying must use the same one. Key rules: Use a consistent config. simple does not stem. Store a generated tsvector for control.

interview.q: Module 23 · Explain Phrase Search in a production query.
interview.answer: The <-> operator requires adjacent lexemes, while <n> allows a distance. Key rules: Use <-> for adjacency. Positions come from tsvector. Stop words can affect phrases.

interview.q: Module 23 · Explain Prefix Search in a production query.
interview.answer: The :* operator matches lexemes with a prefix, useful for search-as-you-type. Key rules: Use :* on the last term. It can be expensive. Combine with ranking.

interview.q: Module 23 · Explain Common FTS Errors in a production query.
interview.answer: Common failures are querying a different configuration than the index, using LIKE for ranking, and forgetting to index the exact expression. Key rules: Match configurations. Use @@ not LIKE. Index the expression.

interview.q: Module 23 · Explain FTS vs LIKE in a production query.
interview.answer: LIKE is simple substring matching, while full-text search handles stemming, stop words, ranking and large documents. Key rules: LIKE is literal. FTS is linguistic. FTS scales with GIN.

interview.q: Module 23 · Explain Practical Search in a production query.
interview.answer: A practical search query filters with @@, orders by ts_rank and returns a headline snippet. Key rules: Filter first. Rank second. Limit the results.

SELECT * FROM courses WHERE to_tsvector('simple', title) @@ to_tsquery('simple', 'sql');
debug.fix: SELECT * FROM courses WHERE to_tsvector('english', title) @@ to_tsquery('english', 'sql');
debug.error: The query configuration does not match the index

debug.title: LIKE instead of FTS
debug.broken: SELECT * FROM courses WHERE title LIKE '%sql%';
debug.fix: SELECT * FROM courses WHERE to_tsvector('english', title) @@ websearch_to_tsquery('english', 'sql');

CREATE INDEX idx_title ON courses (title);
